title: Maximal slicing with locally quasi-finite stabilizer: the slice can be shrunk so that h, s' and t' are flat, finitely presented and locally quasi-finite

statement_spans.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-max-slice-quasi-finite (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 2329-2350

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Take the maximal slice g : U' to U of the max-slice lemma. Since h^{-1}(u) = F'_u and dim_{e(u)}(F'_u) = dim(G'_u) = 0 under local quasi-finiteness of G to U, h has relative dimension at most 0 at (u, e(u)); the local-source-apply remark yields the maximal open U'' of U' containing u on which h has relative dimension at most 0, and after replacing U' by U'' the morphism h has relative dimension at most 0 everywhere. A morphism locally of finite presentation of relative dimension at most 0 is locally quasi-finite (morphisms locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0 lemma), so h, still locally of finite presentation and Cohen-Macaulay, is flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite, proving (4); the restrict-property lemma transfers this to s' and t' of the restriction as base changes of h, proving (5). (source lines 2352-2369)

core_obligations: Take g : U' to U as in lemma-max-slice: h is locally of finite presentation and Cohen-Macaulay with dim_{e(u)}(F'_u) = dim(G'_u), which is 0 since G to U is locally quasi-finite; hence h has relative dimension at most 0 at the point (u, e(u)) (proof lines 2353-2356). Shrink: by remark-local-source-apply there is an open U'' of U' containing u such that U'' times_{g,U,t} R is the maximal open on which h has relative dimension at most 0; after replacing U' by U'' the morphism h has relative dimension at most 0 everywhere (proof lines 2356-2361). Local quasi-finiteness: h is locally of finite presentation of relative dimension at most 0, hence locally quasi-finite by morphisms-lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0; still being locally of finite presentation and Cohen-Macaulay, it is flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite, proving (4) (proof lines 2361-2366). Transfer: s' and t' of the restriction are flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite as base changes of h by lemma-restrict-property, proving (5) (proof lines 2366-2368).
proof_roadmap: Start from the maximal slice of lemma-max-slice and read off relative dimension at most 0 at (u, e(u)) from the vanishing stabilizer dimension (proof lines 2353-2356).
Shrink to the maximal open U'' on which h has relative dimension at most 0 via the local-source-apply remark (proof lines 2356-2361).
Conclude local quasi-finiteness of h from relative dimension at most 0, completing (4) with flatness and finite presentation (proof lines 2361-2366).
Transfer the three properties to s' and t' via the restrict-property lemma, proving (5) (proof lines 2366-2368).
